Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

gay adjective and noun

homosexual

also homosexual, lesbian, gay man, gay woman

modern

M-O s.v. homosexual, gay (after Suet. Galb. 22: libīdinis in marēs prōnior)

amōris in proprium sexum prōnior

adjectival phrase: prōnus, comparative prōnior

drawn to one’s own sex: gay

Morgan–Owens’s phrase, built on Suetonius. For a man amōris in marēs prōnior, for a woman amōris in fēminās prōnior (M-O). In conversation a plain clause says it as well: virōs amat, fēminās amat. Classical Latin has no neutral word; the old sense of English gay, cheerful, is hilaris or laetus (see cheerful).

Other words

  • cinaedus, cinaedī m. — classically a term of abuse

    noun, second declension · avoid · classical · Catull. 16.2 (Lewis & Short); Juv. 2.10 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    An insult in Plautus, Catullus and Juvenal, and so also a lewd dancer (Lewis & Short); never a neutral word for a gay man.

See also cheerful, love.
